Roadmap

Pass Sections
framework vectors, bases, matrices, systems, rank (1–7)
core tools orthogonality, least squares, determinant, eigenvalues, SVD (8–14)
applications numerics, statistics, optimisation, dynamics (15–19)

Always check dimensions first: A is m\times n, x\in\mathbb R^n, b\in\mathbb R^m.
slides.title: Roadmap

slides.html:
Invertible, for Square A

All equivalent: \operatorname{rank}A=n · \ker A=\{0\} · columns form a basis · Ax=b uniquely solvable · \det A\ne0 · 0 not an eigenvalue.

Change of basis: [T]_B=B^{-1}AB (similarity). Use a solver, not A^{-1}.
slides.title: Invertible, for Square A

slides.html:
QR, Weighting, Ridge

  • QR: R\widehat x=Q^Tb — more stable than normal equations
  • weighted: A^TWA\widehat x=A^TWb
  • ridge: (A^TA+\lambda I)\widehat x=A^Tb, unique for \lambda>0
slides.title: QR, Weighting, Ridge

slides.html:
Spectral Theorem

Real symmetric A=Q\Lambda Q^T: real eigenvalues, orthonormal eigenvectors.

\lambda_{\min}\le\frac{x^TAx}{x^Tx}\le\lambda_{\max}
slides.title: Spectral Theorem

slides.html:
Pseudoinverse and Low Rank

  • A^+=V_r\Sigma_r^{-1}U_r^T: minimum-norm least-squares solution x_*=A^+b
  • best rank-k: \|A-A_k\|_F^2=\sum_{i>k}\sigma_i^2, \|A-A_k\|_2=\sigma_{k+1}
  • example: x_1+x_2=2\Rightarrow x_*=(1,1)^T
slides.title: Pseudoinverse and Low Rank

slides.html:
Conditioning

\kappa_2(A)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}}{\sigma_{\min}},\qquad \kappa_2(A^TA)=\kappa_2(A)^2
  • small determinant ≠ ill-conditioned (10^{-8}I has \kappa=1)
  • prefer QR or SVD to normal equations
  • conditioning vs stability vs identification
slides.title: Conditioning

slides.html:
Quadratic Optimisation

  • \nabla(x^TAx)=(A+A^T)x; \nabla\frac12\|Ax-b\|^2=A^T(Ax-b)
  • f=\frac12x^THx-c^Tx, H\succ0: minimiser Hx=c
  • constraints Cx=d: KKT system
  • min-variance weights w_*=\dfrac{\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1}{\mathbf1^T\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1}
slides.title: Quadratic Optimisation

slides.html:
Running Case

A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}, b=(1,2,2)^T: rank 2, no exact fit; \widehat x=(\frac76,\frac12)^T; residual =-\frac16(1,-2,1)^T\in\ker A^T.

Column space, rank, null space, projection, least squares and identification in one example.
slides.title: Running Case

slides.html:
Common Pitfalls

Wrong Right
pairwise non-proportional ⇒ independent fails for \ge3 vectors
AB=0 ⇒ A=0 or B=0 zero divisors exist
symmetric ⇒ positive definite check eigenvalues
nonzero eigenvalues ⇒ diagonalisable only means invertible
echelon columns span \operatorname{Col}A take original pivot columns
slides.title: Common Pitfalls

slides.html:
Self-Check

  1. solving Ax=b = combining columns
  2. null space = unidentifiable directions
  3. least-squares residual ⟂ column space
  4. orthonormal bases simplify projections
  5. eigen for iteration, SVD for rectangular
  6. covariance is PSD; PCA = top eigenvector
  7. invertible ≠ reliably solvable
slides.title: Self-Check
